Diego (AE): Heads-up: Lumenex procurement just pushed back. Exec wants three hard requirements before C-suite signoff for the POC: 1) direct HSM peering (FIPS 140-2), 2) private peering for egress (customer gateway), 3) a timeboxed latency commitment during peak tests. Need internal quick-sync.
Mei (SE): Acknowledged. Quick clarifying Q: do they require raw key material stay in their HSM (no import) or will they allow key import into cloud KMS?
Diego (AE): They want keys to never leave their HSM—so live peering/crypto ops on their side.
Ravi (Presales): Reality check: We have worked customers with HSM export/import and with cloud-KMS BYOK flows. Live HSM peering (RPC to on-prem HSM) is not in our standard offering. It will need engineering + security + legal signoff and an ops runbook. For a pilot we could propose a short-term guarded alternative: KMS proxy that routes signing to their managed HSM via a secured tunnel (requires certs and a mutual TLS config).
Nora (SRE): From SRE side: peering + 1k qps peak changes the topology. Recommended: Dedicated pool with 3x GPU nodes and a warm-up canary, plus NLB in front with private VPC peering. Baseline perf from internal lab for rw-v2-large (seq64): p50=52ms, p95=135ms. At 1k qps expect p95 to drift ~30-40% unless we enable aggressive batching and kv-cache.
Eve (Security): Security caveats: live HSM peering increases attack surface; we need a network diagram, threat model, and an attestation of their HSM vendor (FIPS cert). Also require MTLS mutual auth, IP allowlist, and a signed agreement on crypto responsibility. I'll start a risk assessment doc.
Tomas (Legal): Legal: Live crypto peering will probably need a specific crypto addendum and insurance/indemnity language. For a POC we can offer a limited-scope addendum with liability caps, but need details.
Diego (AE): They also asked for a POC SLA during the 2-week pilot: p95 latency <= 250ms and 99.5% availability. Can we even ballpark operational risk?
Nora (SRE): 99.5% during a short controlled pilot is doable if we control capacity and routing. But availability tied to customer HSM peering adds third-party risk. Recommend a fallback plan: if peering degrades, auto-failover to a cached-response mode (short TTL) or to a soft-degraded model (smaller footprint model). We should surface these trade-offs with the customer.
Mei (SE): Cost question for sales: what's the delta for Dedicated reserved for a 2-week pilot vs hosted consumption? If we assume 3xA100 equiv for 2 weeks, it's materially higher. I can run numbers if someone confirms configuration.
Ravi (Presales): Suggested pilot timeline to show to Lumenex on the bridge: Day 0-2: contract + network prep; Day 3-5: HSM connectivity tests (mutual TLS cert exchange); Day 6-9: perf runs + tuning; Day 10: exec bridge for final signoff. We'll propose a hard freeze period for tests.
Eve (Security): Action: I'll request their HSM vendor certs and request they complete the HSM attestation form. Also need their network engineer contact for IPs and firewall rules.
Tomas (Legal): I'll pre-draft a short crypto addendum template and flag the insurance clause. Diego, send me procurement's initial redlines if any.
bridge-bot: Created ticket SLS-24098: "Lumenex POC - HSM peering + private egress + pilot SLA" assigned to eng-oncall. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SLS-24098
Diego (AE): Can we do an exec bridge tomorrow 9:00am PT? Customer urgent.
Nora (SRE): 9:00am PT works for SRE. I'll join with a short ops checklist and fallback plan.
Mei (SE): I can do 9:00am PT. I'll bring a one-page diagram of the proposed network flow and the KMS proxy alternative.
Ravi (Presales): I'll put together the bridge agenda: 1) ask recap (2m), 2) HSM approach options (8m), 3) network/peering steps (7m), 4) pilot SLA & fallbacks (6m), 5) next steps + owners (2m).
Eve (Security): I'll join for the attestation and risk summary.
Tomas (Legal): Standby; will join if any contractual items are requested during the bridge.
Diego (AE): Owners: Mei -> network diagram + KMS proxy option; Nora -> ops checklist + perf baseline; Ravi -> bridge slides + timeline; Eve -> attestation + risk outline; Tomas -> crypto addendum draft. I'll coordinate with the customer and send the calendar invite.
Mei (SE): Note for internal slides: include `--kv-cache=true` and `--batch-policy=aggressive` as recommended knobs for pilot perf.
Nora (SRE): Running a quick staging run tonight; I'll post the smoke-run snippets here. Command: `./smoke_test --model rw-v2-large --concurrency 1000 --seq 64 --kv-cache`
Ravi (Presales): Also prepping a short runbook for their networking team showing cert exchange steps for MTLS.
Eve (Security): Requesting Lumenex SOC contact email to send attestation form. Diego, pls share.
bridge-bot: Reminder scheduled: exec-bridge (Lumenex) at 2025-06-02T16:00:00Z
Diego (AE): Thanks team. Customer wants speed but won't bend on crypto controls. Let's make the HSM path explicit and show the alternative that short-circuits to a cloud-KMS guarded flow if peering is blocked.
Mei (SE): Filing cost delta calc now and will post numbers by 8:30am PT.
